newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia wheat exports hit record 2.4 MT in March.
newsitem.headline: Australia wheat exports hit record 2.4 MT in March.

text.p: Australian wheat exports jumped to a record 2.4 million tonnes in March, boosting the country's balance of payments by A$500 million, Australian Wheat Board (AWB) managing director John Lawrenson said on Thursday.
Describing the performance as "staggering", Lawrenson said March shipments were 200,000 tonnes better than the previous monthly best set in February this year.
Australian wheat exports would be worth just over A$4 billion for 1996/97 (October-September), he said in a statement.
This was a greater value than any previous crop, even taking into account the smaller but higher-value export crop in 1995/96, which was worth A$3.75 billion, he said.
This year's 23.5 million tonne record crop had resulted in a series of other records, the latest being wheat exported in March, he said.
They included record sales into new markets, record wheat loadings and unstinting efforts in the industry, he said.
December shipments of 1.8 million tonnes were followed by a record 2.1 million tonnes in January, 2.2 million tonnes in February and the 2.4 million tonnes in March, he said.
New markets continued to be developed and South America was expected to buy more than 200,000 tonnes of Australian wheat this year, having bought 170,000 tonnes so far, he said.

"We are also well on track in South Africa, where deregulation is coming up. They have a good crop but we expect to be doing business there later this year and to continue to expand into that region," he said.
Lawrenson said record sales to Iran and Indonesia had been made and these markets were expected to grow.
India had already bought 1.3 million tonnes of Australian wheat and was "talking about more", he said.
Record sales had been achieved without any purchases by China, which this year had a good crop of its own but which normally would buy one to two million tonnes a year, he said.
Nigeria was a new market for Australian wheat, Sudan was doing regular business with the AWB and 100,000 tonnes of durum had been sold to North Africa and Europe, he said.
AWB had also sold and would soon ship about 500,000 tonnes of wheat to Yemen.
"That signals a solid return to this market where our involvement has been fractured by subsidised wheat sales from the U.S. and Europe in recent years," he said.
Turkey would also buy 500,000 tonnes of Australian wheat this year. That was another new market which had responded to targeted promotional strategies, he said.
AWB additionally had sold 2.8 million tonnes of freight so far this year, he said.
AWB was 70 percent committed for the record crop just four months into the selling programme, "a fantastic achievement", he said.
"A lot of what is not priced is earmarked for regular buyers and we are well ahead of schedule," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
